preamble: Primary FSGS  |  Podocyte-intrinsic injury from immune dysregulation, circulating permeability factor, or germline podocyte gene mutation  |  Points reflect diagnostic weight. Cost: Small = standard labs/exam  |  Medium = genetic panel ($200–$1,500)  |  Large = renal biopsy ($3,000–$10,000+)

questions.question: Is proteinuria in the full nephrotic range (urine PCR >3.0 mg/mg or 24-hr protein >3.5 g/day)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — nephrotic-range proteinuria confirmed; hallmark of primary FSGS with diffuse podocyte injury

questions.question: Is there hypoalbuminemia (<3.0 g/dL) with peripheral or generalized edema on physical exam?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — nephrotic syndrome confirmed: heavy proteinuria + hypoalbuminemia + edema triad

questions.question: Is onset acute or subacute (weeks to months) in a child or young adult without an identifiable secondary cause?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — age-appropriate abrupt onset consistent with primary podocyte injury or circulating permeability factor

questions.question: Is gross hematuria absent? (absence supports FSGS over nephritis; microscopic hematuria may be present)
questions.confirmingAnswer: Confirmed absent — no gross hematuria; supports nephrotic rather than nephritic pattern

questions.question: Is focal segmental glomerulosclerosis confirmed on light microscopy (segmental sclerosis in <50% of glomeruli)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — FSGS pattern confirmed by pathologist; DEFINITIVE histologic diagnosis

questions.question: Is the FSGS variant tip, NOS (not otherwise specified), or cellular on light microscopy? (these variants favor primary over secondary FSGS)
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — tip or NOS/cellular variant confirmed; strongly associated with primary immune-mediated FSGS; steroid responsiveness higher in tip variant

questions.question: Is foot process effacement diffuse (>80% of the glomerular capillary surface) on electron microscopy?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — extensive diffuse foot process effacement confirmed; pathognomonic for primary podocyte injury or circulating permeability factor

questions.question: Is immunofluorescence negative or shows only nonspecific IgM/C3 in sclerotic segments (no dominant immune deposits)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — IF negative or nonspecific; confirms primary FSGS and excludes immune-mediated GN (lupus, IgAN, MPGN)

questions.question: Has genetic testing identified a pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant in a podocyte gene (NPHS1/nephrin, NPHS2/podocin, CD2AP, WT1, TRPC6, INF2, ACTN4)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — P/LP podocyte gene variant confirmed; genetic FSGS; steroid resistance expected; cascade family screening indicated

questions.question: Are two APOL1 high-risk alleles (G1/G1, G1/G2, or G2/G2) confirmed in a patient of African ancestry? (collapsing variant association)
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — APOL1 high-risk genotype confirmed; strongly associated with collapsing or NOS variant of primary FSGS

questions.question: Are serum C3 and C4 complement levels normal? (normal complement excludes immune-complex GN; supports primary FSGS)
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — C3 and C4 normal; complement-mediated GN excluded

questions.question: Are oval fat bodies or fatty casts present on urine microscopy (lipiduria)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — oval fat bodies or fatty casts confirmed; reflects heavy urinary lipid loss in nephrotic syndrome

questions.question: Is serum albumin <2.5 g/dL (severe hypoalbuminemia from urinary losses)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — severe hypoalbuminemia confirmed; reflects massive urinary protein loss characteristic of primary FSGS

questions.question: Has the patient been trialed on corticosteroids (prednisone 1 mg/kg/day x 4 weeks minimum) and is the response (complete, partial, or steroid-resistant) documented?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — steroid trial documented; steroid resistance (no remission after 4 weeks) is a defining feature of primary genetic FSGS; steroid sensitivity supports MCD vs. FSGS distinction

high.label: 🔴  80–100 High confidence
high.action: Primary FSGS confirmed; initiate corticosteroid trial if not done; steroid-resistant cases: add calcineurin inhibitor (tacrolimus or cyclosporine) ± MMF; consider rituximab for steroid/CNI-resistant disease; sparsentan (FDA approved 2023) for persistent proteinuria; genetic testing mandatory in all pediatric and young-adult cases

moderate.label: 🟡  50–79 Moderate confidence
moderate.action: Probable primary FSGS; renal biopsy required for confirmation and variant classification; avoid immunosuppression until histology confirmed; rule out minimal change disease (diffuse FPE without segmental sclerosis on LM) which may precede or mimic FSGS

low.label: 🟢  <50 Low confidence
low.action: Primary FSGS insufficiently supported; consider secondary FSGS (perihilar variant, sub-nephrotic proteinuria, BMI >30, prior nephron loss) or alternative glomerular disease; ensure EM is performed to assess foot process effacement extent before concluding
